title: JavaScript Error Handling Core Check
description: Check your understanding of try/catch, finally, throwing errors, built-in error types, custom errors, and practical error handling boundaries.
author: DailyCoder

options.text: Handles errors thrown while the `try` block is running
Prevents all future asynchronous errors automatically

questions.explanation: `try...catch` catches errors thrown during the synchronous execution of the `try` block.

questions.prompt: What happens to the rest of a `try` block after an error is thrown?

options.text: It is skipped and JavaScript jumps to `catch`

questions.explanation: When an error is thrown, normal execution stops and control moves to the nearest suitable `catch` block.

options.text: After `try`/`catch`, whether success or failure happened

questions.explanation: `finally` runs after the `try`/`catch` flow regardless of whether an error occurred.

questions.prompt: Which value should you usually throw?
questions.explanation: Error objects provide useful properties like `name`, `message`, and `stack`.

questions.prompt: Which property usually contains a human-readable explanation of an error?
questions.explanation: `error.message` contains the message passed to the Error constructor or generated by the engine.

questions.prompt: What type of error usually happens when using a variable that was never declared?
questions.explanation: A `ReferenceError` occurs when JavaScript cannot find a referenced variable name.

questions.prompt: What type of error usually happens when calling a method on `undefined`?
questions.explanation: A `TypeError` occurs when a value exists but is used in an invalid way for its type.

questions.prompt: Which error type can `JSON.parse("{ bad json }")` throw?
questions.explanation: Invalid JSON text has invalid syntax, so `JSON.parse()` throws a `SyntaxError`.

questions.prompt: How do you create a custom error class?
questions.explanation: Custom errors are commonly implemented by extending the built-in `Error` class.

questions.prompt: What should a custom error constructor usually call first?
questions.explanation: A custom error class that extends `Error` should call `super(message)` to initialize the parent Error behavior.

questions.prompt: Which check handles only a specific custom error type?
questions.explanation: `instanceof` checks whether the error object was created from a specific class or subclass.

questions.prompt: Where should errors usually be caught?

options.text: Where the code can respond meaningfully

questions.explanation: Catch errors at a boundary where you can log, show a message, provide a fallback, retry, or add useful context.
